The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testMinpackJennrichSampson()` fails potentially due to an issue in the LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer class related to ignoring the VectorialConvergenceChecker parameter. The current bug report explicitly states that LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer ignores the VectorialConvergenceChecker parameter, making it hard to specify custom stopping criteria, which aligns with the symptom.

Exploration of the code snippets revealed that the constructor and various methods related to convergence checking in LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer are ambiguous or have multiple overloads, preventing precise insight into where the vectorial convergence checker is set or used internally. The default constructor sets some default tolerances but does not show handling of a custom VectorialConvergenceChecker explicitly.

The issue likely arises because the optimizer either does not store or use the custom VectorialConvergenceChecker passed to it, resulting in it ignoring user-provided custom stopping criteria. This means when `optimize` is called, it might internally use some default convergence checking mechanism rather than the user-supplied one.

Hence, the root cause is that the LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer does not properly integrate or utilize the VectorialConvergenceChecker parameter passed by clients, causing it to ignore custom convergence checks and rely on defaults.

This explains why the test `testMinpackJennrichSampson()` fails if it tries to use a customized convergence checker. The defective handling of convergence checker stops the optimizer from correctly stopping as expected, leading to test failures.

No recent bug reports strongly add to this diagnosis; they are unrelated or only tangentially related.

The next step is to fix LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer to correctly store and use the given VectorialConvergenceChecker passed to it.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
